batchName: Empire: Diocletian and Constantine (AD 284-337) - Easy Batch 2

questions.question: In what year did soldiers tear down the new church at Nicomedia, launching the Great Persecution?
questions.explanation: On 23 February 303 soldiers destroyed the church at Nicomedia and burned its scriptures. The next day an edict ordered churches and holy books destroyed across the empire.
questions.sourceQuote: On 23 February 303 soldiers tore down the new church at Nicomedia and burned its scriptures.

questions.question: What made Diocletian's departure from power in 305 unprecedented?
options: He was the first emperor to step down voluntarily
He was the first emperor to hand power to his son
He was the first emperor overthrown by his Caesar
He was the first emperor exiled by his own army
questions.explanation: Diocletian was the first Roman emperor to resign of his own accord. Maximian resigned the same day in Milan.
questions.sourceQuote: He became the first Roman emperor to step down voluntarily, and Maximian resigned the same day in Milan.

questions.question: Where was Constantine born?
questions.explanation: Constantine was born around AD 272 at Naissus, now Niš in Serbia. His mother was a woman of humble birth.
questions.sourceQuote: Constantine, the emperor who would make Rome Christian, was born around AD 272 at Naissus, now Niš in Serbia.

questions.question: What was Diocletian's name before he became emperor?
questions.explanation: He was plain Diocles until the army hailed him as emperor in 284. He then took the grander name Diocletian.
questions.sourceQuote: His name was then plain Diocles, and his family was humble.

questions.question: Diocletian's retirement palace forms the old heart of which modern city?
questions.explanation: Diocletian retired to a fortified palace on the Dalmatian coast, which is now the old centre of Split in Croatia. Dalmatia was also the province where he had been born.
questions.sourceQuote: Diocletian retired to a fortified palace on the Dalmatian coast, now the old heart of Split in Croatia.

questions.question: Which emperor, near death in 311, called off the Great Persecution?
questions.explanation: Galerius ended the persecution in 311 and admitted it had not worked. Most Christians had escaped punishment, and many pagans disliked it.
questions.sourceQuote: In 311 Galerius, near death, called it off, admitting it had not worked.

questions.question: When Egypt rebelled in 297, which city did Diocletian besiege until it fell?
questions.explanation: Diocletian besieged Alexandria, Egypt's great port, until it fell in 298. The revolt had broken out partly over new taxes.
questions.sourceQuote: In 297 Egypt rebelled, partly over new taxes, and he besieged Alexandria, its great port, until it fell in 298.

questions.question: According to the bishop who wrote Constantine's biography, what words did Constantine see with a cross of light above the sun?
questions.explanation: The bishop's account has Constantine seeing the words 'In this sign, conquer', in Latin 'in hoc signo vinces'. He said he heard the story from the emperor himself.
questions.sourceQuote: While marching, Constantine saw a cross of light above the sun with the words “In this sign, conquer”, usually given in Latin as *in hoc signo vinces*.

questions.question: How did Maxentius die at the Battle of the Milvian Bridge?
options: He drowned when a bridge collapsed
He was executed after his capture
He was killed in single combat
He took poison as his army fled
questions.explanation: As Constantine's troops drove Maxentius's army toward the river, the temporary bridge of boats collapsed and Maxentius drowned. His head was later paraded through Rome.
questions.sourceQuote: The temporary bridge collapsed and Maxentius drowned.

questions.question: Diocletian styled himself 'Iovius' after which god?
questions.explanation: Diocletian took the title Iovius after Jupiter, king of the gods. His partner Maximian took a name honouring Jupiter's helper Hercules.
questions.sourceQuote: Diocletian styled himself *Iovius*, after Jupiter, king of the gods.
